title: Families of the Great Purge
scope: A small research index of family-centred records connected to the 1937–1938 Great Purge in Georgia.

source.name: Public Archive / Soviet Past Research Laboratory
source.rights: Online-resolution materials may be used for non-commercial research and education with attribution. This pilot stores catalogue metadata and links only.

families.summary: A family archive and oral-history collection preserving portraits and memories connected to imprisonment, exile, the Gulag, and later rehabilitation.
families.note: The archive catalogue identifies 42 photographs; the oral history is described at collection level.

families.summary: A collection documenting political imprisonment, exile, resistance to Soviet rule, and the Great Purge through a family-held photographic record.
families.note: The catalogue supplies thematic counts but does not describe every individual relationship; kinship should be verified record by record.

families.summary: Official family papers include the 1956 certificate overturning the 1937 sentence against Mikheil Germanovich Jajanidze for lack of a crime.
families.sourceLabel: USSR Supreme Court Military Collegium certificate
families.note: The family connection represented by the collection should be expanded only after checking its catalogue records.

families.summary: Isidore Kvitsaridze and his nephew Grigol were arrested during the escalation of Soviet repression; both were executed in 1937 after extrajudicial or political proceedings.

people.name: Isidore Kvitsaridze
people.role: publisher and public figure; executed in 1937

families.note: This biography is currently available in Georgian on Archive.ge.

families.summary: A family-contributed group photograph catalogued by the Public Archive under Soviet totalitarianism and the Great Purge.
families.note: The photograph is linked, not reproduced; identification of depicted people requires further research.
